first_prompt:

commits.summary: Summaries S1: code closure digests per target, naming the parts a change touches; shared.rs's shape now resolves dynamic constants
commits.body:
lib/src/closure.rs (new) computes, for a target in a build, what its proof reads as parts with a digest each: every application method it may run (static and special calls by resolution, virtual and interface calls through every class they may dispatch to, lambda bodies, the initializers of the classes involved), every application class involved (superclass chain, superinterfaces, record components, permitted subclasses, fields with access, type, ConstantValue and annotations, class annotations), each virtual or interface call's set of dispatch targets, and the application files for a closure that touches Spring. Closure::changes names which parts differ between two builds, for the change-impact report (S3) and the proof cache's key (S2). The JDK, the tool's models and the binary are left to the canonical claim's ToolIdentity.

Found while building it: shared.rs's shape, the exact body fingerprint the brief starts from, printed a dynamic constant by its bootstrap index without resolving it. javac makes 'case Color.GREEN' in a pattern switch such a constant, so GREEN against BLUE gave equal shapes and shared::identical_closure called the versions identical: a regression check could have reported 'nothing to prove' for a changed body. A test reproduced it first; shape now resolves a dynamic constant through its bootstrap entry, recursively. The change only makes more bodies differ, so it can turn an identical-closure verdict into a proof, never the reverse. The brief's statement that shape is an exact fingerprint of a body was true except for this case.

commits.summary: Summaries S2a: the claim key and the local proof cache, with adversarial invalidation tests
commits.body: spec/cache.rs implements key, lookup and store. The key is the SHA-256 of the canonical claim written canonically (object keys sorted) under a projection version line. The projection knows every claim field by its path: a field it doesn't know, such as one another stream adds, makes the claim uncacheable rather than being left out of the key, and so does a computed part left empty. The cache is a local directory with one record per key. It stores only verified results and refuted ones that carry a witness; storing an unresolved result is an error, and an entry that is corrupt, for another key, or unresolved is a miss. New: closure::version_digest (a version's code as the closures of the target and of the constructors its inputs are made with), and lib/src/proof_cache.rs (the tool identity: the executable's bytes, the JDK's whole release file, the models' digest).

commits.summary: Summaries S2b: equivalence --cache DIR, the proof cache's lookup on the prepared claim and its store of the result
commits.body:
A regression proof under --engine native now takes --cache DIR (lib/src/proof_cache.rs, Regression and Entry). equivalence.rs gets the two calls the summaries brief allows: one lookup once the claim is prepared (the harness generated and the shared callees planned, before any checker runs), and one store before the last return. The canonical claim is built from the preservation contract, the observations, the flags' correspondence, the bounds, the statement's assumptions and domain, the harness's digest, both versions' code closures (the target and every record constructor), and the tools with every setting that can change a verdict. The deadline is left out: it only decides whether a verdict is reached, and an unresolved result is never stored. Under --engine jbmc or auto the claim is uncacheable, with a note, because JBMC's own identity isn't in the key yet.

A verified hit gives back the stored result and statement, marked Outcome.reuse = exact with the claim key and the run it came from, and no checker runs. A refuted hit first replays the stored witness in the harness on both versions as they are now; if it no longer reproduces, the hit is a miss and the claim is proved again. A refutation is stored only when its witness, read back as stored, reproduces in the interpreter. The check's own report (output, proof line, statement, findings, counterexample) is stored beside the record (spec::cache::store_detail). To read it back, statement.rs's types now derive Deserialize (gap_mode is skipped and restored by name, since GapMode is the heap stream's), and the witness types are mirrored in proof_cache.rs.

Verified by 5 new tests in lib/tests/summaries.rs, native checks on small javac builds. A rerun is an exact hit with an equal statement. A different after version, unwinding bound, array bound, scope, gap mode, no models, or no shared callees each miss. A refuted hit gives back the same counterexample, and a stored witness edited to an input both versions agree on is a miss and is proved again. Every argument type reads back from a stored witness; this test found and fixed a null array read back as no value. Under auto, nothing is stored. Skipping the refuted hit's replay, or fixing the after version's closure, makes the matching test fail. Unit tests (183), conformance (9), integration (64), foundations (3) and summaries (27) pass, and the CLI run twice gives a miss that stores, then an exact hit. Shared files changed: equivalence.rs (Options.cache, Outcome.reuse in its 7 literals, the two calls, Confirmed derives Deserialize), statement.rs (Deserialize derives), main.rs (--cache), lib/tests/summaries.rs and lib/README.md. Notes for the reconcile loop: a field another stream adds to Statement must deserialize, and another stream's new Outcome field goes beside reuse in the same literals.

commits.summary: Summaries S3: jvmcontract impact, the claims a change invalidates and the parts of their code that changed
commits.body:
New command jvmcontract impact --before DIR --after DIR, with claims from --target or a --claims file. build.py's claim.json and --plan output serve as they are, with previousSymbol for a renamed method. A claim's code is what its proof-cache key digests: the closures of the target and of the canonical constructor of each record its inputs are made with. Each claim is invalidated (with each closure part that differs, or the reason when the target is gone), unchanged (a cached result is still hit on its code), or unresolved (the first build has no such method). The verdict uses the key's own version digest (closure::digest_of_version, split out of version_digest).

Checked on the recorded examples by the new examples/tools/impact_check.py, run inline in 15 s. For each of the 59 B9 and B11 examples of Crosscut, Quorum and Mica, impact was asked about every claim of the example's app, between the unpatched build and the build with the example's patch. The report is judged against facts read from the class files independently of the closure walk. The rules: the example's own claim is invalidated; every part named lies in a class whose bytes changed; a claim whose class-level reach holds no changed class is unchanged; and a claim is unresolved only where the first build lacks the method. All 59 pass. Across the reports, 170 claims are invalidated, 1123 unchanged and 84 unresolved. The unresolved ones are examples 147-149, whose patches add the Jitter class. Two mutations of impact.rs show the rules can fail: reporting every claim unchanged fails every example's own claim, and invalidating every claim gives 2216 failures.

commits.summary: Summaries S4a: a changed pure helper proved equivalent is one function in both versions of its callers
commits.body:
With equivalence --cache and --engine native, a changed static helper of a narrow kind is checked first as a regression check of its own, on demand within half the caller's time, or found in the proof cache under that check's key. The kind: pure in both versions, integral values only, no exception of its own, no static initializer. A proof over every input makes the helper one function in both versions of the caller's proof, and the caller's statement gains an assumption of kind callee, basis proved, naming the helper proof's claim key, which is part of the caller's own key. A refuted, unresolved or cyclic helper stays as written, with a note. The checks in progress are a stack, so a helper's proof never rests on the proof it is used in. cache::callee_reuse plans a subject's check without running it, and the integration contract's 'summaries reuse of shop.Pricing#discount in shop.Pricing#total' now passes.

Found on the way: under --engine native no callee was ever shared. The stubs went only on JBMC's class path, which costs nothing for an identical callee, because the own checker's hashing makes both calls one circuit, but would leave a proved helper's two different bodies for the solver to relate. Under the own checker the one function is now the helper's new version itself: the previous version's calls are redirected to it (shared::substitute_directory). The proof is exact and needs no refinement.

The brief's applicability check is met by construction, not dropped. Only a helper proof over every input of its parameter types is used, so the assertion at each call is true, and nothing is compared by numeric bounds. A helper proof with a narrower domain (--unchanged-unless, mapped arguments, a relation between results) is refused, since it would need a real assertion at each call.

commits.summary: Summaries S4b: examples 160 and 161, a changed refill helper proved on its own and used in its caller, and its wrong sibling (verification pending)
commits.body:
Examples 160 and 161 put S4's proved helpers on a recorded app. Both check Crosscut's RetryAfter#nanosUntilToken, which is unchanged, and change its helper TokenBucket.lastAfter. In 160 the helper becomes last + (now - last) / period * period. Its own regression proof holds on every input, so the caller is proved with it as one function in both versions; inline, the helper's proof took 0.19 s and the caller's 0.00 s, against 1.2 s for the caller with the helper as written. In 161 the helper aligns the credit to the clock's grid, which is wrong. Its own proof is refuted, it stays as written, and the caller's proof, scoped to the module's precondition, finds a replayed counterexample: a refused client told to wait 1 ns where it was 2. Crosscut's tests pass on both patches.

build.py gains the cache option. An example's approach.cache passes --cache build/proof-cache, a fresh directory in the patched copy that is never kept. The claim's scope says so, only when it is set. The result records each helper the tool offered for a proof of its own (helpers), and the page says what came of it. A callee assumption reads as the helper's proof. expected.sharedHelpers makes the shared helpers part of the expectation. Seven new tests in examples/tools/test_build.py; its 168 tests pass.

Found and fixed in S4a: the callee assumption's text named the run the helper's proof came from (its time and directories). The assumption is in the caller's claim, so two cold runs on the same code gave the caller different keys. It now names the helper's claim only, and a new summaries test (37 in all) checks the keys of two runs from different directories and caches are equal. It failed before the fix. The unit tests (183), conformance (9), integration (64), foundations (3) and summaries (37) pass.

Jobs, both quick (priority 10): 20261107-053635-example-160-a-changed-refill-helper-prov (expected verified, lastAfter shared) and 20261107-053635-example-161-a-refill-helper-aligned-to-t (expected violation, no helper shared). S4, and with it this stream's core, is done pending them; S5 is next.

commits.summary: Summaries S5: refinement per callee, only the stubs a spurious JBMC counterexample rests on are computed as written
commits.body:
Under JBMC, a counterexample found with the shared callees as memo stubs that doesn't reproduce as written used to send the whole proof back with every callee as written. Now the stubs' memo tables are read off JBMC's trace (shared::answers), the two versions are replayed on the counterexample's input with a stub class that gives those answers again (shared::replay_stub), once as found and once per callee with that one as written, and only the callees whose real answers make the versions agree are unstubbed (shared::spurious); the rest stay one function, and this repeats until a verdict stands or no stub is left. When nothing can be told apart, every callee is computed as written, as before. Any subset of the stubs is still sound for a proof and every counterexample is still replayed as written, so the choice decides how much is computed again, never a verdict. The own checker never takes these stubs, so this is for --engine jbmc and auto.

Tests: 3 more in lib/tests/summaries.rs (40 in all): the replay stub (no JBMC needed); two shared callees where the spurious counterexample rests on one, which alone is computed as written while the proof holds with the other still shared; and a real regression still found through the refinement. With the blame ignored, the two-callee test fails. The unit tests (183), conformance (9), foundations (3), integration (64), skill (1) and summaries (40) pass. One run of integration.rs under load failed in the_tools_own_checker_agrees_with_jbmc_on_integer_proofs: the own checker's native check of the pricing rounding refactor, a path the refinement doesn't reach, spent its 600 s deadline in one solver call. It passed alone in 9.9 s and in the next full run.

Shared files: lib/src/equivalence.rs (the stub directory via shared::stub_directory, replay_on over a class path, the refinement loop), lib/README.md, examples/schema/result.schema.json (the shared purpose's description), lib/tests/summaries.rs. The main brief's 'Where it starts from' still says refinement is all or nothing, true at the fork; it isn't this stream's to edit.

commits.summary: Summaries S6: the proof cache's economics on the recorded examples, cold, warm and after four kinds of change (verification pending)
commits.body:
examples/tools/economics.py (new) measures what the proof cache saves on the 61 recorded B9 and B11 examples of the javac apps (8 more are real-world or Box Office). The cache serves 17 of them, the B9 examples the tool's own checker proves. The other 44 are listed with the reason and not run: B9 under JBMC (JBMC's identity is not in the key) and B11 (prove has no cache). The script runs the 17 claims cold on an empty cache, then warm on it. Then, for Crosscut and Mica, it runs one change of each kind (examples/tools/economics/: an unrelated edit, a behaviour-preserving helper rewrite, a representation change, a real regression). Each change is checked rebased (each example with the change beneath it on both sides) and as its own claims on the served targets, each set cold and warm. Per run and claim it reports how the claim was served (exact hit, nothing to prove, a changed helper's proof found or made in the run, proved or refuted again) and the time: wall, checker, the cache's own, the helpers' checks, and the rest. It also checks that every warm verdict is the cold one, and exits 1 when an expectation fails.

For the times, lib/src/proof_cache.rs notes how long a check's key and lookup took. The note is this run's even on an exact hit, and is never stored. Each changed helper's own check is timed in a note too. Tests: two existing summaries.rs tests gain assertions (40 pass), and examples/tools/test_economics.py (new, 11) covers note parsing, which claims are served, and the whole sequence of runs and expectations against a fake jvmcontract. It also shows the expectations fail when a warm verdict differs or a warm rerun proves again. economics.py --plan built all 90 trees inline (17 s). jvmcontract impact confirms each change reaches the claims it was meant to, and both helper rewrites' own proofs hold (0.06 s and 0.22 s). The unit tests (183), conformance (9), foundations (3), integration (64), skill (1), summaries (40) and test_build.py (168) pass. build.py is unchanged, and so are the recorded results.

Also fixes this brief: S5's commit had spliced its Progress in at the '- Status: working' the Status rule quotes, leaving a second copy of that rule's tail and of the old Progress. Outside Progress the brief is again as before S5. With S6, all of this stream's phases are done, and the Status is done.

Verification pending: job 20261107-064135-the-proof-cache-s-economics-on-the-recor (verification/jobs/), a long job, for review: it should exit 0 with every expectation in examples/tools/economics/report.md met.
